memory_support.text: See the whole front, then return.

prompt.text: Ken has passed a truck. When may he move back in front of it?

answer.text: Only when the truck's whole front shows in his mirror.

This lesson covers the side, front and rear No-Zones, stopping and turning, truck limits, and passing.

Big rig side blind zones swallow cars that ride unseen in the truck driver's mirrors. Tailgating the rear of a truck blinds both drivers to trouble ahead. So hold real following gaps behind a truck. Trucks crawl uphill, swing wide, brake long and tip tall. Human error by car drivers can still wreck the truck driver who swerves to avoid them. The rule is to shun every No-Zone. So stay out of the side blind zones, do not tailgate, and keep a real following gap behind every truck. After passing, reenter only when the full front of the truck shows in your mirror, and do not slow down. Never wedge beside a truck making a wide swinging turn. The manual gives blind areas of twenty feet in front and two hundred feet behind. So to restate: rigs need doubled stopping room, so no cut ins; reenter only when the full front shows in the mirror; and never wedge beside a wide turn.

narration.text: Pass a truck only when there is room, and do not speed to do it. Check your mirrors first. Pass only where passing is legal. Clear the cab briskly. Reenter on the right only when your mirror confirms it. Keep a sustained pace after the pass. So the steps are room, no speeding, checked mirrors, legal ground, brisk cab clearance, a mirror confirmed return to the right, and a steady pace afterward. To repeat: pass with room and without speeding, clear the cab briskly, return only when the mirror confirms it, and do not slow down.

To restate: in front, reenter only when the full front shows in your mirror; behind, hold real following gaps, because tailgating blinds both drivers to trouble ahead.
